usedStatements: Rotating anodes use a tungsten stem to reduce weight.
Rotating anodes allow higher tube currents by distributing heat over a larger area.
The heel effect is greater with a larger anode angle.
Detectors with high detective quantum efficiency require lower patient doses for a given image quality.
A high grid ratio improves scatter rejection but decreases patient dose.
The equivalent noise index NI is a measure used to set tube voltage modulation in CT.
Flying focal spot technology improves sampling and resolution in CT.
Third generation scanners use a rotate-rotate geometry with a parallel beam.
Water‑equivalent phantoms are used to calibrate CT numbers.
A high pitch always results in gaps in helical CT data leading to poorer image quality.
Functional MRI primarily relies on changes in blood flow velocity.
The chemical shift between fat and water at one point five Tesla is approximately 220 Hz
T2 of cerebrospinal fluid is shorter than that of muscle
A rectangular field of view is achieved by using different sampling in frequency and phase directions
Multi echo spin echo sequences collect multiple echoes after a single excitation using a single 180 degree pulse.
The spatial pulse length is equal to the number of cycles in the pulse divided by the wavelength.
Reverberation artefacts occur when echoes bounce between two strong reflectors.
Frame rate increases when the number of scan lines increases, all else equal.
Mirror artefacts occur due to strong reflectors causing duplication of structures behind the reflector
Reverberation artefacts occur when sound is absorbed by a single strong reflector.
Lutetium-177 emits only beta particles and no gamma rays.
LSO and LYSO crystals contain lutetium and have higher light output and faster decay than NaI(Tl).
The sensitivity of a collimator is inversely proportional to the square of the hole diameter
A narrower energy window setting reduces the amount of scattered photons detected in a gamma camera.
The effective half life of a radiopharmaceutical is determined by either its physical half life or its biological half life, but not both.
